# DSH OpenCode Model Sync
Keep the DSH model picker in sync with the **live** OpenCode Go model catalog.

DSH ships its provider catalog as a build-time snapshot. When OpenCode publishes
a new model — say `

kimi-k3.1-pro` — the model exists on the endpoint but the
picker does not list it until a new DSH bu

ild ships. This plugin closes that gap:
it fetches the catalog from `opencode.ai` and writes the res

ult into the
`llm-pi-ai` settings section, so new models appear after a sync instead of after
a rele

into the
`llm-pi-ai` settings section, so new models appear after a sync instead of after
a release.

- No DSH rebuild, no `app.asar` patching, no custom protocol code.
- Startup sync, periodic refresh,

and a manual agent tool.
- Writes only the three provider routes it owns; every other provider and

credential is left untouched.
- Idempotent: an unchanged catalog produces no settings write.
中文说明
## Requirements
| Requirement | Notes |
| DSH Desktop / runtime with `llm-pi-ai` | Built and tested against DSH Desktop 44.7.0 (`@deepseek-a

i/dsh-desktop@0.2.1-rc.5`). |
| An OpenCode API key | Defaults to the `OPENCODE_API_KEY` environment

variable or the DSH credentials entry of the same name. |
| The `llm-pi-ai` provider row | Present
in the default profile as the `opencode-go` route. |
The plugin never reads the key value into logs, tool output, or settings.
## Install

Release archives are produced by `npm pack` and attached to GitHub Releases as
`dsh-opencode-model-s

ync-<version>.tgz`. See the
latest release.
### From Plugin Manager

1. Download the `.tgz` from the latest release.
2. Install it as a bundle. With an agent that has Pl

ugin Manager, use
`install_bundle` with the downloaded file's absolute path (or with the
unpacked di

rectory). The same action works from DSH's plugin UI where a local
package path is accepted.
3. Enab

le the bundle when asked. DSH applies it immediately when HMR is
available; otherwise restart DSH.
### From a checkout

## What it creates

The plugin groups the live catalog by wire protocol and maintains three
provider routes under the `l
lm-pi-ai` settings section:
| Route | DSH protocol | Endpoint from the catalog |

| `opencode-go-chat` | `openai-completions` | `https://opencode.ai/inference/go/openai/v1` |
| `open

code-go-anthropic` | `anthropic-messages` | `https://opencode.ai/inference/go/anthropic/v1` |
| `ope
ncode-go-responses` | `openai-responses` | `https://opencode.ai/inference/go/openai/v1` |

Each route carries its models, context/output limits, image support, and
reasoning levels translated

from the catalog. Models served over protocols DSH
cannot speak (currently `generate-content` for G
emini models) are skipped.

The bundled `opencode-go` route is **not modified by default**. DSH's adapter
takes the wire protoco

l at the route level, so a live catalog that spans three
protocols cannot be represented by one prov

ider route without dropping its
session header and compatibility quirks. Leaving the bundled route i

ntact means
an existing default model selection keeps working while the synced routes take
over disc

overy of new models. Set `retireBundledRoute`
when you want the duplicate gone.
## Usage

Select any model from **OpenCode Go · Chat Completions**, **OpenCode Go ·
Messages**, or **OpenCode

Go · Responses** in the model picker. New catalog
entries show up after the next sync.
### Manual sync with the agent tool
The plugin registers one tool:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- `status` — last attempt/success, last error, the live model count of each
generated route, and how

the live catalog compares with DSH's bundled one.
- `sync` — fetch the catalog now. Only changed ro

utes are written.
- `remove` — delete the three generated routes from settings.
## How it works

1. Resolve the API key through `ctx.credentials` (falling back to the Host
process environment).
2.

`GET <modelsUrl>` with a bearer token.
3. Translate every `type: chat` record by its protocol: limit

s →
`contextWindow`/`maxTokens`, image modalities → `input: [text, image]`,
reasoning levels → `reas

oningEfforts` (`none` becomes `off`).
4. Group records into one route per supported protocol and add

the
`x-opencode-session` header plus DSH's `thinkingFormat: deepseek`
compatibility switch on Chat

Completions.
5. Compare with the current `llm-pi-ai` provider values and call
`ctx.settings.update('

llm-pi-ai', …)` only when something changed.
6. Retry once on network errors, HTTP 429, and HTTP 5xx

; a managed route whose
protocol disappears from the catalog is unset in `retiredModels: drop` mode.

Two safety rules keep the write narrow: the plugin refuses to overwrite a
same-named provider whose

wire protocol differs, and it only removes routes it
can identify as its own.

The write goes through DSH's settings service, so the profile patch stays
human-readable and the pi-
ai adapter rebuilds on the next request.
## Known limitations

- **Cost is not synced.** DSH's provider configuration has no cost field; synced
models report zero

cost in the usage panel.
- **The bundled `opencode-go` route remains by default.** While DSH ships a

n
older snapshot, the same model can appear under both the bundled route and a
synced route. Enable

`retireBundledRoute` to remove it.
- **One session id for every conversation.** Generated routes are

hand-declared
providers, and only the bundled catalog provider receives DSH's per-session
`x-openco

de-session` header. A fixed value satisfies the gateway but may
reduce upstream cache affinity acros

s conversations.
- **Gemini `generate-content` models are skipped** because DSH implements only
`ope

nai-completions`, `anthropic-messages`, and `openai-responses`.
- **Catalog metadata is the only sou

rce.** If OpenCode advertises a wrong limit
or modality, the synced route inherits that error.
